question: The multinational company Ara Shoes Portuguesa, Unipessoal Lda. based in Vila Nova de Gaia is a footwear manufacturer with share capital of EUR 5 million. The Lusa news agency has recently reported on a collective redundancy affecting 130 workers at the company’s Seia manufacturing facility, which has been operating since 1991.

The justification put forward for the mass redundancy was simply ‘adaptation to the market’, but the company has ‘no intention of closing’, according to the local mayor. The company is one of the region’s biggest employers. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission have information on whether Ara Shoes Portuguesa, Unipessoal Lda. has received any EU funds? If so, which?
Is the Commission aware of similar situations at any of the company’s other European production sites?
answer: Ara Shoes Portuguesa, Unipessoal Lda received EU funding from the Operational Programme for the Modernisation of Economic Fabric under the 1994-1999 Community support framework to support the reorganisation of the company’s production process, amounting for a total EU contribution of EUR 387 049.71. The company has not received EU funding since.

The company is not a direct beneficiary under the Portuguese Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP). However, it is member of APICCAPS — Portuguese Footwear, Components, Leather Goods Manufacturers’ Association, which is member of the consortia BioShoes4All that receives RRP funding. The Commission is not aware of similar situations at other European production sites.
To support the workers made redundant, the European Social Fund Plus can provide support for workers to improve their employability through training, upskilling and requalification.

In Portugal, it is mainly the Program Pessoas, Demografia, Qualificações e Inclusão (1) that supports modular training for employees, especially those at risk of unemployment in the context of organisational change and restructuring processes. Moreover, the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund for Displaced Workers (EGF) (2) co-finances active labour market policy measures to support workers in job-transitions.
The EGF may intervene if the Member State submits an application and the criteria defined in the regulation are fulfilled.
